The one thing that matters most

OpenAI launched ChatGPT Images 2.6: it can now make animated GIFs and keep reference images of you, your pets and characters ready to reuse, and two new image models (Flare and Sunburst) reach the API 50% faster.

It is the most-liked watch-list post today (18,674 likes), and creators were already building GIF sprite-sheet games with it overnight. Also: Grok Bot can now make phone calls in the US, OpenAI says its cyber pipeline validated and patched 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities in one run, and Cat Wu is leaving Anthropic to lead product management for Core Products at OpenAI.

Arena.ai@arena · Nov 4

Agent Arena data: Gemini 4 Carbon scales best on cost; for a typical task GPT-6 Astra costs 3.4 times as much and Claude Opus 5.5 3.9 times as much (535 likes).

Models by @GoogleDeepMind scale better on cost than their rivals.

Gemini 4 Carbon is the prime example. As tasks get more demanding, every rival gets more expensive relative to Carbon.

For a typical task, GPT-6 Astra by @OpenAI costs 3.4× as much, Claude Opus 5.5 by @AnthropicAI costs 3.9× as much, and GPT-6.1 Sol is the cheaper option at about half of Carbon’s cost (0.54×).

Across the 5% most expensive sessions, Carbon’s position improves against all three. Opus edges up to 4.2×, Astra’s cost roughly doubles relative to Carbon, and Sol’s discount shrinks.

This in turn can translate into meaningful savings across real-world tasks such as building an Android security app, one of many long-horizon tasks that our Agent Arena users delegate to their agents.

Four models, one prompt to build a working radial engine: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon and Grok 4.7.

this is getting f*cking dangerous. a radial engine has one job - every piston drives the same center, or it spins nothing. no style points.

so I handed the same prompt to four models and watched what they actually built.

Claude Opus 5.5 · GPT-6 Astra · Gemini 4 Argon · Grok 4.7

pistons fanned out like a star, rods all reaching for one hub. four takes on the same machine - and every one bet on a different idea of what “connected” even means.

I didn’t touch the outputs and I’m not scoring them. you’ve got eyes: which one could actually turn over, and which one’s just a pretty pinwheel?

Opus, Astra, Gemini or Grok?

Anthropic's biology team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life (4,111 likes).

Anthropic@AnthropicAI
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: anthropic.com/research/inves…
